arguments.message: Supervise exec command groups and classify post-start failures
arguments.title: Fix exec lifecycle accounting and descendant cleanup (#50)
arguments.body:
Closes #50.

Before changing code, `TestExec_InheritedPipeWaitFailureIsNotStartFailure` reproduced the bug: a shell exited 0 while a descendant held its pipe open, and the tool reported `process_start_failed: exec: WaitDelay expired before I/O complete` with no effect. The tool now distinguishes actual start/process state from wait failures, reports unknown effects for post-start capture failures, marks incomplete output, and signals its process group on cancellation/timeout (TERM then KILL after 200ms) or after an inherited-pipe failure. It reaps the leader; it does not sandbox or promise to contain deliberately detached descendants. Explicit timeouts over two minutes remain usable. The human `!` shell's lifecycle is unchanged except for sharing the status helper's new ProcessState argument. v0 §9/§14 now describe only the implemented scope.

Offline verification on macOS: `gofmt -l` (empty), `git diff --check`, `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` (cmd: no tests; internal/reagent: ok, 16.547s). Focused cancellation/timeout/inherited-pipe regressions passed 3 runs. `GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` passed; Linux runtime tests were not run. No live model run or API spend. `exec` still cannot supervise processes that leave its group; bounded disk log artifacts can already be made with shell redirection and read with read_file, so no new log API was added.

arguments.message: Continue long runs with bounded in-run compaction
arguments.title: Continue long runs across context boundaries (#49)
arguments.body:
Closes #49.

Add a separate within-Run compaction at a settled pre-request boundary; do not reuse manual `Session.Compact`, which clears blocking and starts a separate trace. v0 §10.4 now states the 40%-window trigger (last usage or next-request estimate), 16k headroom, at most eight transitions, step accounting, immutable current task/plan outside the summary, summary validation, and explicit stop on failure/unknown window instead of retries or replay. Summary requests and transitions are traced inside the same Run; usage, call IDs, effects, launch permissions, plan/read-only restrictions and manual/between-turn compaction behavior remain intact. The model is instructed to carry exact checkpoint/verification references; semantic fidelity is model-dependent, so a final report must not treat `completed` as task-verified without evidence.

Tests use scripted offline model responses and a small injected window to force repeated boundaries without large fixture files. They cover two handoffs, an applied tool executed exactly once, call-ID retention, OpenAI/Anthropic encoding, blank/oversized/refusal/tool/provider/overflow/cancelled summaries, actual cancellation, step and transition budgets, no speculation with unknown usage/window, plan/read-only authority, and large trace records. The chat warning test still measures the last request rather than turn total.

Verified locally: gofmt -l (empty), git diff --check, go build ./..., go vet ./..., go test ./... (internal/reagent 20.871s), go test -race ./... (40.915s), make tty-check (all 13 existing scenarios passed). No live model/API run; terminal UI code was unchanged, so no new pty scenario. Within-run continuation cannot salvage a first request that already overflows or infer the window of an unknown model.
